data.narrative:
Gallatin AI is a seed-stage Defense & Security company founded by Woody Glier, Daniel Buchmueller, and Brian Ballard, having raised $15M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 10 comparable companies—2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms including UFORCE, Anduril Industries, Helsing, Castelion, and Shield AI.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses total capital raised ($15M) as a proxy base value and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $38M. The peer-median method examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—UFORCE ($1.0B seed), Singularity ($400M series A), and NODA AI ($125M series A)—producing a median implied valuation of $400M, with a range spanning $125M to $1.0B.

These methods triangulate to a valuation range of $32M (low) to $460M (high), with a median of $219M. The substantial spread reflects two key uncertainties: methodological divergence between stage-based and peer-benchmarking approaches, and inherent dispersion within the defense-tech peer set itself. The stage-progression method anchors conservatively to capital deployed, while peer comparables suggest meaningfully higher value if Gallatin's competitive positioning and technology trajectory warrant defense-sector multiples. Conviction in any point estimate hinges on additional diligence regarding product maturity, customer validation, and differentiation relative to the named peer cohort.
